findings.trigger_condition: A large stream such as [(i, [i]) for i in range(n)], where each integer is hashable and each list is unhashable and unequal to all registered values.
findings.root_cause: Every lookup of a hashable value scans all registered unhashable IDs (lines 82-87), while every lookup of an unhashable value scans all registered hashable IDs (lines 65-70). With both categories growing, registration performs quadratic cross-registry equality checks.
findings.impact: The identity registry has O(n^2) construction time for valid inputs containing many hashable and unhashable nodes, causing severe performance and resource problems on large edge streams despite the graph algorithm itself being near-linear.
findings.suggested_validation: Run dependency_layers([(i, [i]) for i in range(10000)]). The expected result is 10000 two-node layers or equivalent valid layering, but registry construction performs approximately quadratic cross-category comparisons and can become impractically slow.
